newsitem.title: USA: Firm seeks Conrail poison pill changes.
newsitem.headline: Firm seeks Conrail poison pill changes.

text.p: Wyser-Pratte & Co Inc said Monday it intends to seek an amendment to Conrail Inc's bylaws which would encourage the company to be more responsive to the views of shareholders.

The New York City broker-dealer said it proposes that antitakeover defenses, such as Conrail's poison pill, would have to be terminated after 90 days unless shareholders approved directors' opposition to an offer.
Wyser-Pratte said its proposal would apply to defenses against premium cash tender offers, including the pending offer by Norfolk Southern Corp for Conrail.

Under the firm's proposal, it said, if Conrail's board determined it could not redeem the poison pill because of its existing merger agreement with CSX Corp, the by-law would require approval of any combination with CSX by a majority of Conrail's disinterested shareholders in addition to any other vote that might be required.

The firm said it plans to introduce its proposal at Conrail's next annual meeting. The railroad has not announced the date of its next meeting, Wyser-Pratte said, noting the meeting has been held in May in the past.

"Conrail is attempting to coerce its shareholders into approving the CSX offer, which brings significantly less value to shareholders than the opposing Norfolk Southern bid," the firm's statement explained.
